name: Real socialism
summary: Real socialism, also called actually existing or developed socialism, is the Soviet-bloc order as its own ruling parties defended it from the Brezhnev era: a single party guided by Marxism-Leninism, state and cooperative ownership under central plans, guaranteed work, housing and health care, and an atheist, secular state. It presented the existing system as a mature stage on the road to communism, not a model to be replaced, and held that the bloc must stay united, as in the Brezhnev Doctrine. Critics inside and outside the bloc, such as Rudolf Bahro, used the same phrase to point at the gap between official ideals and practice.
scope: The Soviet-type regimes of the Eastern Bloc from the 1960s to the late 1980s as defined by the 1977 Soviet Constitution, the doctrine of developed socialism and the Brezhnev Doctrine, answered as an adherent of the ruling parties. It excludes Maoist and Titoist variants, post-1989 reform socialism and dissident critics of real socialism, who used the term sarcastically.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Article 42 guarantees free, qualified medical care from state health institutions as a citizen's right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Article 40 promises pay not below a state-set minimum and Article 23 commits the state to raising pay and real incomes, so a rising wage floor fits.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Article 16 makes state plans the basis of economic management, and markets are not credited with allocating resources better.

public-ownership.rationale: Articles 10 and 11 make state property the principal form and list industry, transport, banks, utilities and land as state-owned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Article 14 has the state set tax rates on taxable income, but large private wealth is barred by design, so heavier taxes on the rich are not a doctrinal theme; adherents are indifferent.

unions-good.rationale: Article 7 gives trade unions a role in managing state and public affairs, though as party-led bodies rather than independent bargaining agents.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 13 protects only personal property and bars property from being used for unearned income; Article 10 makes socialist ownership the foundation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No private corporations exist under Articles 10 and 11, so tighter regulation is inferred from the state's total control of enterprise.

cut-welfare.rationale: Articles 40 to 45 make work, housing, health, education and old-age support state-guaranteed rights, which are the system's main claim to legitimacy.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership sits with the state (all the people) and with collective farms and cooperatives, not with each firm's own workforce; work collectives only take part in decisions under Article 8.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The security organs were extensive in the bloc and defended as protection of the socialist system; the sources do not discuss terrorism specifically.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Article 65 demands intolerance of anti-social behaviour and public order; drug liberalization is not part of the model, inferred from that.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Articles 36 and 52 make advocacy of racial or national exclusiveness and religious hostility punishable by law.

strong-leader.rationale: Official doctrine stressed collective party leadership (Article 6), though a general secretary dominated in practice; adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: The preamble keeps the state as the instrument for building communism, and Article 31 calls its defence a main function; abolishing it is a distant goal at most.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; an armed-forces monopoly and a tightly controlled state suggest strict gun limits, inferred from the security-minded system.

empower-police-military.rationale: Article 31 stresses constant combat readiness and Article 32 commits the state to supplying the forces with everything necessary.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Article 60 treats evasion of socially useful work as incompatible with socialism and Article 65 requires intolerance of anti-social behaviour; the bloc criminalized or suppressed prostitution.

decide-locally.rationale: Article 3 puts democratic centralism in force, so lower bodies must observe higher decisions, and Articles 74 and 75 give all-Union law priority; local initiative is permitted inside that frame.

rehabilitation.rationale: The official line spoke of re-educating offenders toward socially useful labour, but the sources read do not detail penal doctrine.

traditional-family.rationale: Article 53 puts the family under state protection and the state encourages childrearing, but the model also demands full equality of spouses, so support is moderate.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The bloc states criminalized or ignored homosexuality, and marriage is defined in Article 53 as between woman and man.

abortion-legal.rationale: Article 35 and the system's emphasis on women in work and legal protection of mothers fit the permissive abortion law actually in force in most bloc states.

more-religion-public.rationale: Article 52 separates church from state and school from church and protects atheistic propaganda.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Article 36 bans racial privilege and the state backed anti-racist and anti-colonial causes abroad, but domestic remedies of this kind were not a theme of the system.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources emphasise legal equality of women (Article 35) and say nothing on the nature of gender, so adherents are indifferent.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Article 27 commits the state to preserve society's cultural wealth and Article 36 allows use of native languages, while nationalist exclusiveness is condemned.

gradual-change.rationale: Real socialism treated its own order as the settled outcome of revolution and sought only gradual perfection (Andropov's stage to be perfected), while condemning reformist deviations from it.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Article 38 grants asylum to left-leaning foreigners, but migration was tightly state-controlled; no sources address reducing it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Article 29 pledges respect for international law and cooperation but the state defended its own sovereignty; split between support for the UN and bloc primacy.

free-trade.rationale: Article 30 prioritizes socialist economic integration and the socialist international division of labour, with state monopoly of foreign trade in practice.

nation-first.rationale: Article 30 places the state within a socialist community with internationalist duties, while Article 62 also demands strengthening the state's power; the bloc line favoured socialist internationalism over narrow national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Article 29 asserts non-intervention in internal affairs, though the bloc intervened to defend socialist rule; the rights-based rationale is not endorsed.

open-borders.rationale: Article 33 and the bloc's practice of controlled exit under citizenship law show that borders were tightly controlled, even if world communism is a distant goal.

limit-growth.rationale: Article 15 sets as the supreme goal of production the fullest possible satisfaction of growing needs through dynamic growth of productivity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Article 18 mentions protecting the environment but not climate; the issue was not part of the doctrine and adherents have no settled view.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Articles 15 and 21 rely on scientific and technological progress and mechanisation to raise productivity and remove arduous labour.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The bloc built nuclear power widely and prized technological progress; the sources read do not mention nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: The preamble celebrates the October Revolution and Article 28 supports national liberation, but real socialism treated its own order as achieved and discouraged revolutions against bloc governments.

experts-over-public.rationale: Article 6 has a party armed with Marxism-Leninism set society's course in a planned, theoretically substantiated way, and Article 26 organizes science for planning.

central-planning.rationale: Article 16 requires management by state plans for economic and social development combined with enterprise initiative.

socialized-markets.rationale: Article 16 uses profit and cost as levers within a plan but the system rejected a market alternative; Article 17 only permits small individual labour.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is state property under Article 11, so a tax on land value makes no sense; the idea was never part of the doctrine.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Article 13 explicitly protects the right to inherit personal property, though large private fortunes were not allowed to exist.

basic-income.rationale: Article 14 ties reward to the principle of work and Article 60 makes work a duty, so an unconditional income conflicts with them.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The state held a foreign-trade monopoly and protected its planned economy from the world market, inferred from Articles 16 and 30.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Articles 11 and 16 give the state the basic means of production and have it direct development through plans.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Articles 10 and 13 make socialist property dominant and cap personal property to small holdings and consumption goods.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition is a communist aim in the doctrine, but Article 14 and Bahro's critique show wage labour and money were retained under developed socialism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Article 11 lists the banks as state property under the plan, so central banking sits at the heart of the system.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Articles 7 and 8 involve unions and collectives in management but under party leadership, not as bodies setting wages and prices with employers.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 6 names the CPSU the leading and guiding force and nucleus of the political system, armed with Marxism-Leninism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The preamble records the overthrow of capitalist and landowner rule and Article 2 vests power in the people through soviets.

democracy-best.rationale: The system claimed a superior socialist democracy (Articles 2, 9) and directed it through the party; it did not accept that voters may freely choose badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Article 5 provides referendums on major matters but they were rare in practice; adherents are split between formal endorsement and party guidance.

workers-councils.rationale: The soviets are the political foundation (Article 2) but are party-led under Article 6; adherents claim soviet power while ruling out independent councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 72 gives each Union Republic the right freely to secede, though Article 74 subordinates republic law to all-Union law.

natural-rulers.rationale: The state is the instrument of the working class and Article 34 bars distinctions of origin; adherents reject natural aptitude for rule as an idea.

political-violence-never.rationale: The state was founded in revolution, maintained security forces and intervened in bloc states, so pacifism about political violence was not held.

war-builds-character.rationale: Article 28 bans war propaganda and pledges peace; the state celebrated war heroism but did not endorse war as character building.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 52 states that the church is separated from the state and the school from the church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Article 52 separates church and state, and Article 6 bases policy on Marxism-Leninism rather than scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Articles 31 and 32 make defence a state function and the courts are state bodies.

military-superiority.rationale: Article 31 requires constant combat readiness, and Article 32 supplies forces with everything necessary; the bloc pursued parity with the West.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Article 36 bans advocacy of racial or national exclusiveness and the Soviet people were defined as multinational.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The preamble reads history through revolution and classes, though it declares class antagonism ended in the USSR.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Article 14 applies the principle of reward by work, not equal pay, even as Article 19 aims at elimination of class differences.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Autonomous regions and areas exist in the federal structure, but land is state property under Article 11; the issue is not part of the doctrine.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Article 28 supports national liberation and the bloc backed anti-colonial states, but the sources do not mention reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Article 30 binds the state to a union of socialist countries based on ideology and internationalism, not religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Article 10 says no one may use socialist property for personal gain, and the preamble's law of life is concern of all for each.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Article 59 says the exercise of rights is inseparable from duties and Article 39 says rights must not harm society or the state.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Article 18 protects nature as a resource for present and future generations, an instrumental framing.

limit-population.rationale: The bloc leaned pronatalist (see Article 35 support for mothers); no source argues for active limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Article 22 and the preamble celebrate industrial development as the material basis for communism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Article 15 stresses scientific and technological progress, while the system was wary of disruption to the party-led order.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; the bloc was suspicious of such individual liberties and the question was marginal in its ideology.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Soviet planners were interested in cybernetics, but the doctrine offers no stance on AI taking over government decisions.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The security state controlled communications; inferred from Article 6 party control, not from a stated position.

restore-past-order.rationale: The preamble describes the revolution as a break from past oppression and a progression toward communism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Article 6 requires Marxism-Leninism to determine policy, so ideological fit comes before pragmatic results, though real socialism also justified itself by results.

direct-action.rationale: The regimes ruled through party and state bodies and treated independent mass action against them as hostile, as in Poland 1980-81 (Brezhnev Doctrine).

means-match-ends.rationale: The state used coercive methods to build the egalitarian goal, with the party leading from above; adherents did not accept that means must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The preamble celebrates powerful productive forces and rising well-being through development.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Article 19 aims to eliminate the essential distinctions between town and country and mental and physical labour, but only as a distant aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The preamble names the classless communist society as the supreme goal and Article 14 treats reward by work as the socialist stage before it.

production-for-use.rationale: Article 15 states that the supreme goal of social production under socialism is the fullest satisfaction of people's needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The preamble says the USSR ended exploitation of man by man and Article 14 speaks of labour free from exploitation, implying private profit is exploitative.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The preamble says the dictatorship of the proletariat was necessary but its aims are fulfilled and the state became one of the whole people, so adherents treat it as a completed stage.

collective-farming.rationale: Articles 10 and 12 make collective farm property a main form of socialist property, with the state promoting its approximation to state property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Soviet line held imperialism to be the source of war, while Article 28 added that war could be prevented by peaceful coexistence.

taxation-theft.rationale: Article 14 has the state set tax rates and the system rests on state revenue; the claim is foreign to the doctrine.

harm-principle.rationale: Article 39 limits rights when they harm society or the state, a wider test than harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article 39 grants individual rights but Article 7 and Article 36 recognise collective and national bodies, and duties to the community come first.

conscription.rationale: Article 31 institutes universal military service and Article 63 calls it an honourable duty.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Article 33 and the bloc's exit controls show that leaving a country was restricted, while participation was the official ideal.

state-as-business.rationale: Article 10 forbids use of socialist property for personal gain; the state serves the people, not as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Articles 40 to 46 ground rights in guaranteed work, housing, health and education, i.e. material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Article 6 holds that the party leads all state and public organizations, so the media and universities are party instruments, not rival powers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Article 36 asserts equal rights and punishes racial exclusiveness, and the doctrine stresses environment over heredity.

organic-representation.rationale: Article 7 lets unions and public organizations take part in state affairs, but the party-state does not use bodies like families and communities as representation in place of parties.

total-state.rationale: Article 6 has the party direct society and Articles 25 to 27 have the state direct education, science and culture, though Article 13 and 17 leave personal and family spheres.

national-rebirth.rationale: The preamble presents the order as an achievement of a developed society rather than needing a rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Article 29 pledges inviolability of frontiers and territorial integrity, though the bloc expanded its sphere through influence.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Article 3 grounds rule in elected, accountable bodies under democratic centralism, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The preamble ends exploitation and Article 40 guarantees the right to choose trade and job.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Article 6 requires Marxism-Leninism as the guide of all social life and class-based critique of bourgeois science.

universal-morality.rationale: Soviet ethics rested on communist morality tied to class (Article 8 communist morality), not universal moral truths known by reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The preamble holds a society where concern of all for each prevails and the party sets the general perspective, with no balancing of class interests inside.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The bloc was officially anti-Zionist, though Article 29 supports self-determination, so Zionism was condemned as bourgeois nationalism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the constitution; Article 33 leaves citizenship to law and the bloc treated diasporas as foreign.

revive-national-language.rationale: Article 36 allows native languages to be used, but the system promoted Russian as the common language and was not committed to reviving lost ones.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Article 8 has work collectives take part in deciding enterprise matters, though with party oversight, so the vote is consultative.

school-vouchers.rationale: Article 25 sets up a uniform, state system of public education and Article 45 makes education free.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Plans, not market budget rules, set spending in a socialist economy; deficit worries were not central but sound planning was valued.

economic-freedom.rationale: The system held that political freedom rested on socialist ownership and rejected economic freedom as a precondition.

rule-by-example.rationale: The state ruled through law (Article 4) and the party, though communist morality and personal example were also stressed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Article 29 affirms equal rights of peoples and their right to decide their own destiny, but the right was subordinate to bloc discipline.

force-without-un.rationale: The bloc intervened in Czechoslovakia and Afghanistan without UN approval, justified by its own doctrine.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Article 6 enjoins Marxism-Leninism as a scientific guide, and Article 52 grants atheistic propaganda.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Articles 40 to 45 grant social rights to citizens, while Article 37 gives foreigners only rights provided by law.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Article 60 makes work an obligation and Article 14 says socially useful work determines status; parasitism was a punishable offence.

class-collaboration.rationale: The preamble says class antagonism has ended and classes are drawing together, but doctrine rejects collaboration with capital elsewhere.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Article 27 commits the state to protect and make use of society's cultural wealth.

dominated-front.rationale: Article 28 supports peoples' struggle for national liberation and Article 30 builds a socialist community counter to the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Article 30 and the preamble put socialist internationalism at the centre.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 35 gives women and men equal rights and Article 53 makes spouses completely equal.

ban-interest.rationale: Article 13 permits earned savings and state banks (Article 11) paid interest, so a legal ban on interest is inferred as unlikely.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 36 makes limits on rights on grounds of race punishable by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The preamble calls the Soviet state the instrument of the revolution, but declares it now a state of the whole people, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The bloc was a major exporter and user of oil, gas and coal and prized industrial growth.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Article 36 allows native languages and bars national exclusiveness, but the system promoted a unified Soviet people.

elite-replacement.rationale: Article 36 punishes national hostility, and the conspiracy is foreign to the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Article 95 elects deputies by direct vote to Soviets, and with the CPSU as the only party under Article 6 there are no party lists to apportion; adherents reject the idea of party-proportional seats.

national-mission.rationale: Article 28 backs world socialism, and the USSR saw itself as leader of a model to be followed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The doctrine held that women's legal and economic equality was achieved (Article 35), but acknowledged remnants; adherents deny the structural claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Article 49 bans persecution for criticism but the doctrine portrayed the party as serving the people; critics such as Bahro said the bureaucracy was a privileged layer.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Article 53 protects the family and the doctrine opposed eugenics as fascist.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The security organs were party-controlled and unaccountable to outside bodies; the doctrine did not call for accountability for past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Articles 10 to 26 give the state a large economic, social and cultural role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Article 36 bars racial privilege and Article 53 treats marriage as based on free consent.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Articles 34 and 36 guarantee equality before the law regardless of origin, race, sex, or religion.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The preamble claims a socialist society was created in the USSR and calls developed socialism a stage on the road to communism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The doctrine opposed colonialism but the sources do not take positions on settler states, apart from the bloc's hostility to Israel.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Article 34 guarantees equality before the law irrespective of religion and Article 52 separates church from state.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 52 protects the right to profess or not profess religion, though practice restricted religious activity.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No religious restriction on cattle slaughter fits a state that excludes religious law from the legal order.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Article 52 states that the school is separated from the church.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Articles 31 and 32 make defence a primary state function, and the state of the whole people is not set to wither soon.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Article 2 declares that all power belongs to the people through the soviets, though Article 6 puts the party above them.

trade-surplus.rationale: Planned foreign trade aimed at needed imports, not surplus accumulation as a goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Article 36 forbids hostility on national grounds, but forced deportations in Stalin's time are a historical blemish the doctrine disowned.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state defended collective ownership by force and protected socialist property by punishment under Article 61.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Article 8 promotes socialist emulation and cooperation instead of competition between individuals and peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Article 6 bars any party but the CPSU and the doctrine defended that monopoly against anti-socialist forces.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The doctrine does not use this concept; the bloc claimed freedom from capitalist domination but not from the state.

separated-powers.rationale: Article 2 makes soviets supreme and Article 3 democratic centralism, which rejects checks among separate branches.

vanguard-party.rationale: Article 6 and the preamble describe the CPSU as the vanguard of all the people, with a leading role that has grown.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The bloc claimed to have abolished poverty and put workers first, so a priority for the poor was not a distinct theme.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Article 11 keeps most urban housing as state property, though Article 44 supports cooperative and individual building.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were not recognised in the Soviet system and independent labour action was suppressed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Article 14 attributes well-being to labour free from exploitation, not to population, and poverty to capitalist institutions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Article 36 and the preamble present a multinational Soviet people as a strength.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Article 3 prescribes election of all state bodies and Article 107 calls for deputies to be recalled by voters.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Article 39 allows rights to be limited by the interests of state and society, which can license emergency measures.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The planned economy fixed prices of essentials and Article 16 and Article 23 aim at stable living standards.

party-controls-media.rationale: Article 6 puts the party as the nucleus of all state and public organizations, and Article 50 conditions press freedom on the interests of the people and socialism.

party-commands-army.rationale: Article 6 makes the party the leading force of all state organizations, including the forces, the control exercised through political officers.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Article 33 leaves acquisition of citizenship to law; the doctrine had no distinct view on naturalization times.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The socialist ideal of no privileged pay, Article 14 and Article 107 accountability; real privileges existed, which critics such as Bahro noted.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Article 3 and democratic centralism oblige lower bodies to follow the decisions of higher ones.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Article 29 stresses sovereign equality, while socialist integration within the bloc under Article 30 was accepted, but not an EU-style pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Under Article 6 the party, not a head of state, directs all state bodies including the forces and ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Article 52 separates church from state, so the state has no stake in church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Article 52 and the atheistic ideology rule out religious authority over politics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: This was a Leninist stance for imperialist wars; the Soviet state itself defended the motherland as a sacred duty in Article 62.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Article 47 grants freedom of artistic work only in accordance with the aims of building communism, and censorship ensured conformity.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The constitution did not limit the party's general secretary's term; the question of re-election limits had no place in the doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Article 107 says deputies who have not justified their constituents' confidence may be recalled at any time by a majority of electors.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Article 30 binds the state to the socialist community and the Warsaw Pact alliance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Article 44 relies on low rents for state housing and Article 11 keeps most urban housing state-owned.

people-in-arms.rationale: Article 31 establishes armed forces and universal service, not militia replacement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Article 19 and 22 aim to erase the distinction between town and country and raise rural living conditions rather than praising rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The bloc accepted the division of Germany and Korea in practice, though Article 29 affirms inviolability of frontiers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The intelligentsia is one of the three allied groups in Article 1 and 19; anti-intellectual resentment was not doctrine.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Article 36 asserts equal rights for all nations and nationalities, though the Soviet culture was seen as socialist in content.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment remained in the bloc's criminal codes for grave crimes, including treason and terrorism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Article 35 supports gender equality in education, but the bloc was reserved about sex education; adherents are split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Article 52 separates school from church and the doctrine rests on scientific materialism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The bloc banned pornography as bourgeois decadence, and Article 65 requires intolerance of anti-social behaviour.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Article 33 federal citizenship rests on law; the system relied on both republic membership and descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Articles 36 and 45 allow use of native languages and schooling in them.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Article 39 says rights must not harm the interests of society, so special exemptions from general law are unlikely.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Article 65 and communist morality (Article 8) press for conformity with socialist conduct standards.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Article 28 supports peoples' struggle for liberation and the bloc criticized imperialist debt, though the sources do not state the position.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The doctrine sees national liberation as needing social progress and socialist transformation (Article 28).

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was framed by party-led bodies, not an assembly; the 1977 constitution was drafted by a party commission.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Article 39 and Article 50 limit freedoms in the interests of socialism and development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The bloc gave aid to allied states, and Article 28 backs national liberation, yet it did not frame it as a universal duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The USSR held its own arsenal as part of the claim to defence capacity (Article 32).

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Presidium of the Supreme Soviet was elected by the legislature, not directly by the people.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Article 11 makes the banks state property under the plan, so no independence is allowed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Article 29 stresses inviolability of frontiers while also holding peaceful settlement of disputes; the issue is not settled in the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 13 says property must not be used for unearned income or to the detriment of society and Article 10 forbids personal gain from socialist property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The preamble claims a socialist society was created with social ownership of the means of production.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Article 18 mentions protection of the environment but the doctrine does not mention a precautionary principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Article 30 commits the state to comradely mutual assistance, and the Warsaw Pact was a collective defence alliance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The bloc held the Baltic annexation lawful while Article 29 stressed territorial integrity; adherents are split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Article 52 separates church from state, and the system in practice kept religion under state registration and controls.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state came from the ruling party and Article 6 put the party above all state bodies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 72 allows secession in principle, while Article 74 asserts all-Union law and the bloc used force to prevent exit.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Article 74 and 75 hold the territory and the system uniform across the Union.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The doctrine is atheist and Article 52 rejects religion, so rulers are not divine.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Article 14 has the state set tax rates, with the planned economy taxing mostly through enterprises.

character-from-environment.rationale: The preamble stresses moulding the citizen of communist society, assuming character is formed by conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Article 4 and Article 6 say state organisations and party organisations must observe the Constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Article 26 promotes science and the bloc prized its space programme, though the sources read do not call it a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Article 2 vests power in the soviets of the people, with no mixing of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: After Stalin's cult was denounced, Brezhnev-era doctrine favoured collective leadership, though honours for leaders persisted.

equal-parenting.rationale: Article 53 stresses equal spouses but also protects mothers, so no clear position on custody rules.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The preamble says the USSR put an end to antagonisms between classes, so class struggle is not a feature of developed socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land was nationalised in 1917 and collectivised; further redistribution to individual farmers contradicts Article 12.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the bloc supported Palestinian return rhetorically but moved millions of Germans out.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Article 29 insists on inviolability of frontiers and territorial integrity, which excludes co-ethnic claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article 52 grants the right not to profess a religion and the state rejects religion in law.

women-must-cover.rationale: Article 35 and the secular state allow no legal dress requirement on women.

common-currency.rationale: The bloc used a transferable rouble for trade; adherents had no view on a single currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Article 30 builds unity around socialist ideology, not language or ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The state combined federal national republics (Articles 70 to 88) with a unified Soviet people, so the choice is not clear.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The doctrine opposed Zionism and held that minorities should win equal rights where they live, as Article 36 guarantees.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The preamble reads the transition to communism as a stage determined by development of productive forces.

ban-cartels.rationale: No private cartels exist; the state organized industry in planned associations, so the statement is not applicable.

no-bailouts.rationale: The planned system sustained state enterprises with subsidies; that failing firms are let go was not doctrine.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The system had no independent constitutional court, as the 1977 Wikipedia article notes, and the party led; it does not map onto the question.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Soviets reserved places for women in practice and Article 35 secures equal political participation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The bloc sought economic integration inside its own camp (Article 30) but did not aim for autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; foreign trade was state-controlled and conducted in planned agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Article 14 combines material and moral incentives and keeps reward by work, so material incentives remain central.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: This is a foco view; the system's doctrine held that revolution requires objective conditions and party leadership.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Article 34 bars distinctions of origin and the preamble recalls overthrow of landowner rule.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Article 36 promotes Soviet patriotism and internationalism together; the doctrine has no civilizational model.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Article 29 affirms the equality of peoples, and the bloc condemned colonial rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Article 36 and Article 62 call for education in Soviet patriotism and socialist internationalism and loyalty to the motherland.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Article 36 bans privileges on racial grounds but the Soviet system did use national quotas in the republics.

public-money-creation.rationale: Article 11 gives the state the banks, so public bodies control credit and money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The preamble sees the transition to socialism as epoch-making; official doctrine expected a general crisis of capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The bloc extended its influence in the former Russian empire's lands but the doctrine did not present it that way.

delink-world-market.rationale: Article 30 favoured integration of the socialist bloc, and the USSR encouraged developing states to ally with it rather than isolate.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin's theory is part of the tradition but the sources read do not report the bloc's view in the developed socialism era.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article 34 and Article 36 impose equal rights and punish discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution lists rights, but with no court or mechanism to enforce them against the party, per the 1977 constitution article.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Article 29 recognizes the right of peoples to decide their own destiny, but no text addresses treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Article 3 establishes the electiveness of all bodies of state authority from the lowest to the highest.

minority-veto.rationale: Article 3 requires lower bodies to observe higher decisions and minorities to follow majority decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Article 4 requires everyone to observe the law, but resistance to the party-state was not permitted.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Article 2 has the Soviets as political foundation to which other bodies answer, though the party led them.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Article 18 protects the animal kingdom, but the sources read do not discuss animal sentience.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Article 18 mentions rational use of the animal kingdom; humane limits are not stated.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The system abolished privileged classes (Article 34) and relied on state provision, not a duty of the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Article 48 gives citizens the right to take part in state affairs and Article 59 makes participation a duty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The bloc condemned bourgeois mass culture, but used its own media and arts for mobilisation, so adherents are split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramsci's hegemony thesis was not adopted by the Soviet orthodoxy, though some later Marxists used it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Article 28 backs national liberation and Soviet doctrine blamed imperialism for exploitation of colonies.

native-born-offices.rationale: Article 34 bars distinction by origin, but office in practice required party membership.

party-own-road.rationale: The Brezhnev Doctrine held that the ruling parties of the bloc could not challenge the party monopoly or leave the Warsaw Pact.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Article 30 favours mutual assistance among socialist states and Soviet aid to allies.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Article 29 insists on inviolability of frontiers, which rules out claims for lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Article 34 and 36 establish equal rights regardless of origin, which excludes preferred leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The preamble honours victory in the Great Patriotic War, and bloc states such as East Germany founded their legitimacy in anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Real socialism presented itself as the opposite of fascism, rejecting the equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist historiography held the Civil War was driven by slave power versus free labour, in line with historical materialism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The bloc removed monuments to the old order and condemned figures, according to its revolutionary self-image.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The doctrine claimed gender equality already achieved (Article 35), and special male programmes were not a theme.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not a theme in the doctrine; the focus was on protecting mothers and children under Articles 35 and 53.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The doctrine held the Soviet model to apply to all socialist states and sanctioned intervention against divergence.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Article 6 subordinates all state bodies, the forces included, to the party; they guard the motherland, not politics.

paid-care-work.rationale: The doctrine aimed to socialise domestic work (Article 53) and paid mothers' benefits, but not wages for housework.

filial-duty.rationale: Article 66 states that children are obliged to care for their parents.

office-by-exam.rationale: Posts were filled through the party's nomenklatura and Article 3 requires election, not examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Article 11 gives the state ownership of strategic industry, so foreign takeover is excluded.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Soviet family law allowed easy divorce, consistent with Article 53's marriage based on free consent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Article 107 allows deputies to be recalled at any time by decision of a majority of the electors.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Article 43 sets up pensions funded by state social insurance and collective farms.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Article 11 makes land state property, with collective farms holding it in perpetual use under Article 12.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Supreme Soviet formally approved the state plan and budget, though under party direction.

single-official-language.rationale: Article 36 allows native languages in schooling and public life, though Russian was promoted as common language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Article 11 vests all land in the state, so foreigners cannot own land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The doctrine's test of discrimination is legal limits on rights under Article 36, not outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Article 15 promotes satisfaction of growing material needs but also warns against acquisitive attitudes; adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Article 28 supports peoples' national liberation and the bloc armed liberation movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Brezhnev Doctrine explicitly justified sending troops to Czechoslovakia to preserve socialist rule against reform.

corporate-influence.rationale: The doctrine criticised capitalist lobbying, though the question hardly arises in a system without private corporations.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The party-state kept tight control of external contacts and information; Article 62 asks citizens to safeguard state interests.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Articles 35 and 53 provide paid leaves and benefits to mothers and large families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land belongs to the state, so local restrictions on purchases do not arise.

job-guarantee.rationale: Article 40 guarantees the right to work, meaning guaranteed employment and pay.

democratic-peace.rationale: Soviet doctrine held that capitalist democracy breeds imperialism and war, and did not credit democracy with peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Article 59 obliges citizens to observe the constitution and Soviet laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Article 29 states non-intervention, but the Brezhnev Doctrine permitted intervention within the bloc.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet unions were organised by branch of industry, though the sources read do not discuss craft versus industry.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Article 36 punishes advocacy of national hostility.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Article 53 takes marriage and the family under state protection.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Article 9 calls for greater openness and Article 50 for broad dissemination of information, but the system classified much and lacked a right to government information.

local-production.rationale: Article 16 aimed at an integral all-Union economic complex rather than local self-sufficiency.

informal-organisation.rationale: Article 6 and Article 51 assume organisation in the party and licensed public organisations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Article 29 pledges good faith fulfilment of international law, while the state asserted sovereignty; split.

religious-nation.rationale: Article 52 and the Soviet people's multinational definition exclude a religious nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Article 29 affirms sovereign equality of states, though the bloc did require deference to Moscow in practice.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The plan transferred resources across the union, per Articles 16 and 19 on drawing nationalities together.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Article 13 protects personal property from earned income, such as consumer goods, houses and savings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Article 28 pledges peaceful coexistence of states with different social systems, and the doctrine holds communism to be the future, so defeating it is rejected.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Article 24 sets up state systems of health, social security and utilities, with cooperatives as supplements.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats religion as an illusion that will fade (Article 52 allows atheistic propaganda).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism-Leninism credits capitalism with building the productive forces on which socialism builds, as the preamble implies.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Article 35 ties women's equality to employment and state support, a socialist-economy answer.

socialized-care.rationale: Article 53 has the state provide childcare institutions and communal services to ease family work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The system promoted internationalism and borrowed many words, with no language purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet state treated treaties with national groups inside it as superseded by the constitution.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Article 12 allows cooperatives and collective farms but within a centralised state; small self-governing communes are not the model.

majority-settlement.rationale: The Soviet state moved Russians into non-Russian republics but described this as economic development, not majority settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The bloc saw itself as communism-building, and a third course was rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Article 29 rests on inviolability of frontiers and not on historical claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Article 36 and the Great Patriotic War narrative treated Nazi crimes as established fact.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Soviet law criminalized male homosexual acts and most bloc states did the same.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Article 6 reserves leadership to the CPSU and the Brezhnev-era system suppressed dissidents; Article 50's freedoms apply only in the interest of socialism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Article 52 separates church and state, and the state had no concept of blasphemy law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Article 28 supports national liberation and Soviet doctrine condemned colonialism.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The bloc backed Afghan government against Muslim insurgents and the doctrine is secular, but it supported national liberation fighters.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Article 52 separates church and state and the state is atheistic in ideology.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Articles 8, 9 and 48 give citizens a role in workplaces and communities, though through party-guided channels.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine saw class as primary and claimed racism and sexism were solved by socialism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The bloc did not recognise gender identity in law, and homosexuality was a taboo in the doctrine.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; the state protects health and life under Article 42.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine rested on class and the socialist path versus capitalism.

alienated-labor.rationale: The preamble says exploitation ended and labour is free; Bahro argued alienation persisted, so official doctrine would see capitalism as the cause.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Article 36 and Article 52 rule out discrimination on religion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Article 2 states that all power belongs to the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The school and the state were secular under Article 52, so religious dress was not shown; the sources do not discuss dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Article 35 protects women, but the doctrine has no view on NDAs and arbitration that did not exist.

social-market-economy.rationale: Article 16 manages the economy by state plans, not a market framework with social protections.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Article 31 institutes armed forces and universal military service.

rich-first.rationale: Article 14 aims at the elimination of class differences, and Article 19 at social homogeneity; though Deng's China used this model, Soviet doctrine did not.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Article 30 binds the state to the socialist community and the Warsaw Pact.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Article 3 requires election of all state bodies and Article 34 bars distinctions of origin.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit was issued by state banks under Article 11, not by user-owned banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The bloc criticised the IMF as an instrument of imperialism but borrowed from the West in the 1970s and 1980s.

property-franchise.rationale: Article 34 bars distinction by property status and Article 96 gives all adult citizens the vote.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The ecofeminist thesis was not part of the doctrine.

reification.rationale: Marx's commodity fetishism was recognised, but Soviet orthodoxy did not emphasise it; a humanist theme more at home in Western Marxism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Article 50 says press, television and radio are placed at the disposal of the working people and their organizations.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Article 4 requires the state to function on the basis of socialist law, though party directives were also followed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Articles 34 and 96 give every adult citizen the vote and bar distinctions of race or nationality.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in the 1970s; the doctrine of participation (Articles 5 and 48) could extend to it but adherents had no view.

open-government-data.rationale: Article 9 calls for greater openness and publicity, but the system classified decision records.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Article 3 uses elected bodies, not random selection, to give voice to the people.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Article 53 bases marriage on free consent and Article 34 bars distinctions based on religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Article 36 punishes advocacy of national hostility, and private shops hardly existed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The state's atheist doctrine takes no part in religious reform, and the sources do not discuss it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The state held that capitalist concentration of wealth restricts freedoms of the people in the capitalist world; the bloc itself had few private fortunes.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The bloc criminalized homosexuality and Article 63 treats service as an honourable duty not open to open LGBT people.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Article 52 permits atheistic propaganda while church and state are separate; the bloc promoted atheism through its schools, though less so than earlier.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Article 65 and Article 31 stress maintaining public order, and the withering away of the state is a distant goal.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The system rested on party leadership and the federal structure with no grand-coalition form of power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The state is to guarantee health care, work, housing and social security as citizens' rights (1977 Constitution), so relying on charity would contradict the model.

term-limits.rationale: The 1977 Constitution sets no limit on re-election to office and the system kept leaders such as Brezhnev for decades, so limits were not part of it.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: deputies are elected and subject to recall under party-led soviets, but individual delegation of votes by topic is not part of the system.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from the foreign policy articles, which commit the state to preventing war and nuclear catastrophe, not a stated stance on extinction risk generally.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: churches are separated from the state and religion is regarded as a private matter, so the ruling parties had no position on internal church offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The constitution guarantees women equal rights with men in the family and the doctrine requires equality of spouses, so a husband's headship is rejected.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The 1977 Constitution grants the vote to citizens (Article 96), not residents, so local voting for foreigners is inferred as rejected.

rent-control.rationale: The state fixed low rents and Article 44 guarantees housing at low rent, which implies legal rent limits.

abolish-ip.rationale: Article 47 protects authors' and inventors' rights, so abolishing patents and copyrights is contrary to the order.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Pioneers and Komsomol organised drilled youth with a socialist-patriotic training aim; the ideology backed them, though the Constitution mentions it only briefly.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The bloc deployed Soviet nuclear forces on allies' territory under the Brezhnev-era alliance, so keeping them out is inferred as rejected.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Soviet forces were stationed in bloc states under the Warsaw Pact, so opposing foreign bases is inferred as rejected for allies.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The Soviet Union formally condemned Nazi crimes against peoples, so formal recognition is inferred as accepted; not addressed in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Article 14 states the principle 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his work'.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Article 31 calls defending the socialist homeland a sacred duty, so a ban on killing in defence is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Constitution speaks of a new historical community, the Soviet people, which cuts against national continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The official Marxist-Leninist view treated sex as biological; inferred, not stated.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Official doctrine held 'the woman question' within class analysis; inferred rejection of a politics without a stable category.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The state honoured the fallen of the Great Patriotic War as heroes; 'saints' is secular-adjusted, so only a moderate agree.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is materialist and atheist, so politics as spiritual struggle is rejected.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The bloc's internationalism did not make homelands centres for diasporas; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Developed socialism holds that the party-state leads culture and society, so cultural renewal before state is inferred as rejected.

god-not-male.rationale: The state was atheist and neither promoted nor reformed religious language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Official atheism gave religious texts no standing for political judgement; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Articles 34 and 36 guarantee equality of nations and races, so majority control of economic life is rejected.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The 1977 Constitution organises republics, autonomous republics and regions for named peoples, matching territorial units for each people.

independent-unions.rationale: The 1977 Constitution makes the CPSU the leading force and places trade unions under its guidance as one of its mass organisations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The state presents itself as one in which power belongs to the people led by the working class, with the party as its vanguard.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water, health care and transport are state-run public services under state ownership of the main means of production.

second-chamber.rationale: The USSR Supreme Soviet had two chambers, the Soviet of the Union and the Soviet of Nationalities.

municipal-property.rationale: Property was state or cooperative and collective farm owned, not owned by local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic centralism subordinated lower bodies to higher ones, the opposite of coordination without governing.

family-wage.rationale: Pay was set by the state, with equal pay for equal work; the family wage is not stated.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; a centrally planned health system had its own approval bodies.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; state-funded science is inferred but ageing research was not an aim.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the state monopoly over banking and money and central economic planning.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's control over information and its security services.

person-over-state.rationale: The Constitution joins rights to duties and subordinates the individual to socialist society's interests.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The state was atheist and secular and held a materialist view, not a spiritual one.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: the formally federal order was run as a centralised state under one party, so lower powers were derivative.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from faith in science and technology for production; not a stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from developed socialism's push for industrialisation and urbanisation.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Official doctrine treats class and proletarian internationalism as primary and rejects race-based organising.

racial-pride.rationale: Official doctrine stresses socialist patriotism and internationalism over ancestry-based pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Brezhnev Doctrine justified invading bloc members such as Czechoslovakia, so force was not limited to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Soviet model was a multinational union with equal peoples and native-language schooling, so language alone was not the basis of a state; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The constitution gives universal, equal, direct elections to all citizens and separates church from state, leaving no place for religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The bloc line cast Western powers as seeking to subvert and break up socialist states, as in the Brezhnev Doctrine; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Article 45 guarantees free provision of all forms of education, with higher education and state stipends for students.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Article 18 protects nature through state planning and rational use, not taxes on polluters; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Article 18 states that steps are taken to protect the land, water and air in the interests of present and future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Article 35 frames women's role as equal rights plus protection of mothers, not distinct values to be weighted in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Article 28 names universal and complete disarmament as a foreign-policy aim, though the bloc also maintained large forces.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Official line praised open Leninist diplomacy but bloc practice was closed and secret; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The constitution places foreign trade and external economic activity under a state monopoly.

missingStatements.text: The state should declare that its society has reached a stage of mature socialism and treat its existing institutions as that stage rather than as a temporary compromise.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1977 preamble declares that a developed socialist society has been built, a natural stage on the road to communism, and the doctrine defends existing institutions on that basis.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Soviet-bloc doctrine; no other ideology could meaningfully take a side.

missingStatements.text: Socialist states form a community whose members owe one another mutual assistance and may not leave it or abandon their political system.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 30 commits the USSR to socialist internationalism within a socialist community, and the Brezhnev Doctrine held that a threat to socialism in one state threatens all.

notes: The label was sincere in official use and sarcastic in much dissident use. Many answers on cultural and criminal-law questions rest on documented bloc practice or inference and are marked low. Later-era strands such as Gorbachev's reforms would answer differently on markets and party monopoly.
